summary: As of November 9, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.34 percentage points and are down 0.09 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are down 0.03 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 11.11 percentage points. Of the 0.12 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.09 was the credit spread and 0.03 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 4.86 percent as of November 6, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.26 percent as of November 6, 2026, a gap of 0.40 percentage points. Brent is 91.46 dollars a barrel as of November 10, 2026 (-11.72 percent over five trading days), and the curve is an unpublished curve shape. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.25 percent as of November 9, 2026, down 0.14 percentage points over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.63 percent as of November 6, 2026. The broad dollar index is 121.88 as of November 6, 2026, +0.43 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 19.92 as of November 9, 2026. The Fed balance sheet is 6.75 trillion dollars as of November 4, 2026, up 1 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Reserve balances are 2.93 trillion dollars as of November 4, 2026, down 100 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Overnight reverse repo is 0.152 billion dollars as of November 10, 2026, down 0.073 billion over the latest four observations.
